messages.subject: Multiple meanspec plots in the one plot
messages.subject_clean: Multiple meanspec plots in the one plot
messages.body_plain:
Hi guys,
I'm a fairly new user to R and this group (however I've been lurking in the background here for several weeks).

I am currently using an 8 channel wav file, and I would like to compare average frequency spectra of channels 3-8. I've been using meanspec() and am able to bring up 6 different plots, but I would like to have them all in the one plot.

I have seen in another post that ggplot2 is used (post titled "plotting spectra of more than two species in one fig"), however I have not been able to work out how to save the output from each iteration of the loop in order to progress.

Any advice would be greatly appreciated. Code is below.
Cheers
Chris

par(mfrow=c(2,3))
starttime = 1
cl <- rainbow(8)
MCsnippet_in <- readWave(filename="EIN105-1200-160824_T013.WAV", from = starttime-1, to = 1, units="minutes", toWaveMC=TRUE ) #read in file
for (chan_loop in 3:8){
              snippet_in <- Wave(MCsnippet_in@.Data[,chan_loop], samp.rate=96000, bit=24) #read in each channel, one at a time
              meanspec(snippet_in, alim = c(0,0.03), flim = c(0.5,20), col = cl[chan_loop]) #calculate meanspec and give a different colour to each

                }

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

The main problem I can see in your code, is that you currently, run the function meanspec, but you don't actually save the output.

Try adding something like:
spec_data <- data.frame()

right before the start of your loop. This creates an empty dataframe.

Then replace your meanspec(...) line with:
temp <- meanspec(snippet_in, alim = c(0,0.03), flim = c(0.5,20), plot = FALSE)  ## Colour doesn't matter here, and you don't want to plot the data, you want to output the data
spec_data <- rbind(spec_data, data.frame(freq = temp[, 1], amp = temp[, 2], channel = chan_loop))

This will save the output of meanspec to 'temp' depending how you wish to compare the frequency spectrums, you may also want to use the argument 'norm = FALSE', so they are not scaled.

Then it grabs the amplitude, frequency, and channel information, create a new data frame (data.frame()) and then bind it to your master dataframe (rbind(spec_data, ...)).

Then, after the loop is complete you can plot this master dataset with ggplot2:
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = spec_data, aes(x = amp, y = freq, colour = chan_loop, group = chan_loop)) +
geom_point() # OR geom_line()

Let me know how this works for you!

Steffi
--
Dr. Stefanie LaZerte

University of Northern BC
stefanie...@unbc.ca

messages.body_plain:
Hi Steffi,
Thanks very much for the reply. That saves the output for me, exactly what I was after, cheers!

I didn't include the code I was using to try to save the data, as everything I was trying only saved the last iteration (chan8).
I did however finally work out something very similar last night (albeit more crudely). I have included that below.. just because...

I did try opening the data with ggplot2, however, using the code supplied it only shows data from channel 8. Not really an issue though as I can use the data elsewhere in more familiar places like Excel as its saved.

Again, many thanks, I really appreciate it.
Chris

counter = 1
outmatrix<-data.frame(matrix(nrow=12, ncol=512)) #defines a matrix
row.names(outmatrix)<- c("CH3x","CH3y","CH4x", "CH4y", "CH5x", "CH5y", "CH6x","CH6y", "CH7x", "CH7y", "CH8x", "CH8y")

inputname <- "EIN105-1200-160824_T013"
starttime = 1 #start time
MCsnippet_in <- readWave(filename=paste(inputname,".WAV",sep=""), from = starttime-1, to = 1, units="minutes", toWaveMC=TRUE ) #read in file

        for (chan_loop in 3:8){     #loop through channels 3:8

              snippet_in <- Wave(MCsnippet_in@.Data[,chan_loop], samp.rate=96000, bit=24)

                freq_spec <- meanspec(snippet_in, alim = c(0,0.05), flim = c(0.5,20), wl = 1024, plot = F) #generate frequency spectra
                 outmatrix[counter,1:512]= freq_spec[1:512,1]
                 outmatrix[counter+1,1:512]= freq_spec[1:512,2]
                 counter = counter+2

                   }

tmatrix <- t(outmatrix)

spec_filename<- paste(inputname,".csv", sep="")
write.csv(tmatrix, file = spec_filename)
